Maria: Guess what happened today. She rearranged my kitchen again 😠
Manjula: Your mother-in-law? Ugh, tell me everything.
Maria: Threw out half my jars and said I own too many. I've told my friends too, they're horrified.
Manjula: I told Mummy and she says it sounds like disrespect. She might mention it to Bua.
Maria: Wait, please don't. I only wanted to vent
Manjula: Too late, Bua already called your mother-in-law 😬
Maria: Now she is telling everyone I've been shaming the family. My husband barely spoke at dinner.
Manjula: I'm so sorry. I didn't think it would travel.
Maria: It started with jars. Now it's a whole family thing.

qa.q: What does Maria's line "I only wanted to vent" suggest about what Maria wanted?
qa.a: It suggests Maria wanted to be heard and comforted, not to start a family dispute, and Maria now feels worried and regretful as the story spreads.

qa.q: What could Maria do now to calm things?
qa.a: Maria could speak to the mother-in-law directly, say sorry that the story spread, and explain what bothered Maria about the jars, rather than sending more messages to others.

qa.q: How might Manjula be feeling after seeing the result?
qa.a: Manjula probably feels guilty and worried, having passed the story on without thinking about where it would go.

grounding: Maria complains to cousins and friends, the story spreads, and the conflict widens.

In their village near Pala, everyone went to the same church and the same fish market, so news travelled fast.
Ganga had married Thomas two years earlier, and his mother still corrected her cooking, her saris, even how she lit the lamp. It hurt. So Ganga began telling her cousins at the market, and her friends at the tailoring class. Every story got a gasp, and a little comfort.
But her cousin told her aunt. Her aunt told someone from Thomas's side at a wedding. Within a month, people were asking Thomas's mother, "Is it true you make her cry?"
One evening Thomas came home tight-lipped. "Amma heard everything. She says you've shamed the family in front of the whole parish."
His father stopped speaking to Ganga's parents. A small kitchen problem had become a quarrel between two families.
Ganga sat on the verandah steps, wishing she could pull every word back.

qa.q: Where did Ganga tell her friends about her mother-in-law?
What was Ganga feeling on the verandah steps?
qa.a: Ganga felt regretful and ashamed, wishing she could take back what she had told others.

qa.q: What else could Ganga have done instead of telling cousins and friends?
qa.a: She could have talked privately with Thomas about what hurt and asked him to help her speak calmly with his mother.

qa.q: How does the spreading story look to Thomas's mother?
qa.a: Thomas's mother feels publicly shamed and disrespected, hearing about it from others in the parish rather than from Ganga directly.

grounding: It shows a wife telling cousins and friends about her mother-in-law's behaviour until the story spreads, the in-laws feel disrespected and the conflict widens.

In Toronto, Jin's group chat with her college friends was where she went after hard days, and her mother-in-law was giving her plenty.
Every Sunday Min-ho's mother came over and reorganised the kitchen. She said Jin's kimchi was "too Canadian". Jin typed it all to the group. Sofia replied with angry emojis. Others added stories. It felt good to be on the same side as everyone.
Then Jin's cousin shared a screenshot with her own mother, who mentioned it at the Lunar New Year dinner, loudly, in front of Min-ho's aunt.
The next week, Min-ho's mother didn't come. She called Min-ho instead. "Your wife laughs at me with strangers."
Min-ho came home quiet. "Now my aunts are calling too. Why didn't you just tell me?"
Jin looked at her phone, at all those supportive messages, and felt sick. What had been a kitchen problem was now the whole family's business.

qa.q: Where did Jin's cousin's mother mention the screenshot?
qa.a: At the Lunar New Year dinner, in front of Min-ho's aunt.

qa.q: How did Jin feel looking at the supportive messages at the end?
qa.a: Jin felt sick and regretful, seeing that the comfort from friends had turned a kitchen problem into a family-wide conflict.

qa.q: What else could Jin have done with her frustration?
qa.a: She could have told Min-ho first and asked him to help talk with his mother privately, keeping the problem within the couple and the mother-in-law.

qa.q: How might Min-ho's mother feel about what happened?
qa.a: Min-ho's mother feels mocked and disrespected, which is why she stops visiting and tells Min-ho his wife laughs at her with strangers.

grounding: It shows a wife complaining to cousins and friends about her mother-in-law until the story spreads, the in-laws feel disrespected and the conflict widens.
